card.name: Punctuation and links in nursing-mother passages
card.fires_on: A comma, period, or small linking word such as "Because" or "the" right after a statement that a drug may be excreted in human milk, in a Nursing Mothers section.

modes.label: Comma after milk statement
modes.description: A comma following "however" or an animal-study phrase in a lactation passage.
modes.example: It is not known whether simvastatin is excreted into human milk; however<<,>> a small amount of another drug in this

modes.label: Because after milk sentence
modes.description: The word "Because" opening the standard line that many drugs are excreted in human milk.
modes.example: It is not known whether this drug is excreted in human milk.<< Because>> many drugs are excreted in human

modes.label: Linking word in nursing text
modes.description: A small word such as "the" or "of" inside lactation or absorption sentences.
modes.example: Clinical Impact: Colesevelam hydrochloride may decrease<< the>> absorption of fat-soluble vitamins A
